units.unit: Wants to work through the essay's cited sources starting with tenant testimony
Requests the source on Mr Chan, delivery driver in Kwai Chung, rent cap and public housing queue
Requests the document containing Mr Chan's testimony cited as D3
Needs passages covering his situation and views on the cap
These give the tenant-side evidence the essay's first argument rests on
Wants to pull supply-side and legal materials: academic working paper on rent-control supply elasticity
Wants Berlin and New York evidence
Wants Basic Law and enforcement analysis
Elasticity paper is load-bearing evidence for claim that a first-rent cap shrinks entry
Berlin/New York are cases used to show the mechanism in the wild
Legal/enforcement material shows why a cap is the wrong instrument even if wanted
All five carry the supply, comparative, and legal claims the essay builds on
Supply-side and comparative evidence is covered
Remaining cited sources are legal and enforcement documents D9 and D10
From D9 wants how a hard cap on initial rents would be characterized as deprivation of rental income triggering Basic Law compensation
From D9 wants the cap framed as regulation of contractual terms that would survive but leave first rents untouched
From D9 wants the band-based middle option and what infrastructure it would need
From D10 wants the Rating and Valuation Department's staffing estimate for a certifiable tenancy register
From D10 wants evidence about which tenants enforcement would miss
The two remaining sources the argument still needs are legal characterisation and enforcement capacity
Wants to check whether the landlord association's submission engages with the supply argument or just makes a fairness claim
That distinction matters for how to frame the counterargument
Engaging would mean offering its own supply evidence or a direct response to the elasticity estimate rather than just a fairness or hardship claim
Landlord submission tests whether supply argument is engaged or merely asserted
